text:
The hits just keep on coming for Puka Nacua.

One day after the Los Angeles Rams' star receiver was issued a three-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, it was learned that the 25-year-old's season could be in jeopardy.

Rams coach Sean McVay revealed to reporters on Friday, Nov. 20, that Nacua underwent surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, Nov. 17, and will be out a couple months. Nacua, who will serve his suspension on injured reserve, won't have to miss any additional games when he is healthy.

The NFL was not aware of Nacua's surgery prior to announcing the suspension, a league spokesman told USA TODAY Sports.

With just one full month left in the regular season, the receiver's recovery timeline doesn't seem to match up with a return to play this season. If anything, it would appear that Nacua's best chance to get back on the field rests primarily on whether the Rams make the playoffs.

Here's what to know.

Puka Nacua injury update

Nacua underwent surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, Nov. 17 and will miss a couple months, according to McVay.

The receiver was placed on injured reserve by the Rams on Nov. 12 with injuries to his MCL and PCL, which was a change of plans after initial indications were that he'd avoid that fate.

As a result, Nacua was slated to miss a minimum of four games. He already missed one prior to the suspension coming down from the league.

Why was Puka Nacua suspended?

Nacua's suspension comes after a league investigation into his personal conduct stemming from an incident that took place on New Year's Eve last year.

Earlier this year, a woman accused the Rams receiver of biting her on the shoulder on Dec. 31, 2025, causing injury, pain and suffering, according to a lawsuit she filed on March 20. The alleged incident took place after a group dinner in the Century City area of Los Angeles, during which Nacua also is alleged to have made an antisemitic remark.

Nacua has denied the allegations and entered a rehab program in April. He played in the Rams' season opener and seven total games before his IR stint and suspension as the league reviewed the incident.

Can Puka Nacua serve his suspension on injured reserve?

Players are permitted to serve their suspension while on injured reserve.

Nacua will have to forfeit three game checks as a result of the suspension, however. He also can't practice or attend games, something that would be considered unlikely after surgery anyway.

USA TODAY Sports' Jack McKessy and Jacob Camenker contributed to this report.

title: Uncovering CTE risk in former NFL players - Concussion Alliance
description:
CTE is a degenerative brain disease found in individuals who have sustained repeated blows to the head and can only be diagnosed after death.
CTE is most prevalent in high-contact athletes, first responders, and the military, and is rare in the general population (about 1%).
This study builds on previous research estimating that at least 25% of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE, as well as responses to that research.
The study sample included 2,362 deceased NFL players, including brain donors (396) and non-donors (1,966).
In other neurological diseases, these skills start to erode five to seven years before diagnosis, and CTE may be similar.
text:
This article was initially published in the 11/19/26 edition of our Concussion Update newsletter; please consider subscribing.

Julia Gallini and colleagues at Boston University's School of Public Health published a study in JAMA Network Open estimating that almost 75% of the 2362 former National Football League (NFL) players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) neuropathology. CTE is a degenerative brain disease found in individuals who have sustained repeated blows to the head and can only be diagnosed after death. CTE is most prevalent in high-contact athletes, first responders, and the military, and is rare in the general population (about 1%).

While ~75% of this group had CTE neuropathology, a smaller subset, 27.2%, had been diagnosed with all-cause dementia during their lifetime. Helio author Shawn Arraj spoke with lead author Gallini, who "emphasized that the [CTE] prevalence estimates do not reflect the percentage of deceased NFL players who showed symptoms of CTE while alive…A portion of these players likely had no noticeable symptoms while they were alive, and another portion was likely experiencing only mild symptoms." This study builds on previous research estimating that at least 25% of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE, as well as responses to that research.

A CBS News article added a caveat to the study. Dr. Kristen Dams-O'Connor, the director of the Brain Injury Research Center at Mount Sinai, said "the results of the paper 'cannot and should not be interpreted as being representative of current living athletes.'" In the last few years, the NFL has made rule changes to try to decrease the likelihood of concussions. Dr. O'Connor also noted that "the results could not be applied to the 'vast majority of people who played youth football' or other non-professional contact sports."

The study sample included 2,362 deceased NFL players, including brain donors (396) and non-donors (1,966). Out of the donors, the researchers found that 93.5% had CTE. To account for selection bias, the researchers calculated that individuals are 5 times more likely to arrange for brain donation if they experienced negative symptoms in their lifetime, resulting in the 74.5% prevalence estimate and a conservative lowest estimate of 63.7%

CTE is often thought to have a silent phase, with unidentifiable changes happening in the brain. However, Dr. Jay Alberts, director of the Cleveland Clinic Concussion Center, notes that some changes may be identifiable. He says that "what we need to do is listen more carefully and use better measurements to understand what those changes are." These measurements could include daily skills, such as driving and balancing a checkbook, that require both cognitive and motor skills. In other neurological diseases, these skills start to erode five to seven years before diagnosis, and CTE may be similar.

Ongoing studies are trying to identify biomarker changes associated with CTE. A study site at UT Health San Antonio is following current and past players and evaluating their brains and behaviors to identify any abnormal changes. In the last 10 to 20 years, there have been rapid advances in Alzheimer's therapies, and researchers are hoping to translate these findings to many other neurodegenerative diseases like CTE.

On Thursday, the NFL and NFLPA agreed on the terms of a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy that would coincide with the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver's stint on injured reserve for PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe injuries.

One day later, the Rams revealed Nacua might not play again this season.

Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL injury and could miss at least a couple of months, putting even a return for the postseason in jeopardy. The 2023 fifth-round pick is in the final season of his rookie contract and is set to enter free agency in 2027.

Read More on NFL

More News: Vikings Front Office ‘Doesn’t Like’ Their 1st-Round Rookie ‘At All’

Nacua injured the MCL in his right knee and a toe in the Rams' 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on November 8. Nacua leads the Rams with 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven game appearances and seven starts this season. The Rams' second-leading receiver, Davante Adams, remains on injured reserve after he ruptured his hamstring in Week 6.

Los Angeles has a big decision to make on Nacua before free agency begins in March, and certainly Nacua's off-the-field issues could come into play during negotiations.

Nacua has faced several controversies, including an incident last December in which he made a gesture associated with antisemitic stereotypes during an online livestream. He later apologized, saying he did not understand its meaning. In March, a woman sued Nacua, alleging he bit her arm and made an antisemitic remark during a New Year's Eve gathering. He also spent time at a holistic rehabilitation facility during the offseason and acknowledged previously misusing alcohol.

Nacua, 25, made a big impact on the Rams in his first season in the league, setting the NFL rookie receiving yards record in 2023. Through 51 regular-season games, Nacua has caught 383 passes for 4,906 yards and 23 touchdowns.

Last week, McVay told reporters the Rams initially expected to keep Nacua on the 53-man roster, though the receiver was expected to miss an "extended period of time" while he recovered from the injuries. Los Angeles wound up needing the roster spot for wide receiver Brennan Presley, and had to put Nacua on injured receiver as "things changed."

"We didn't need (the roster spot) initially," McVay said of placing Nacua on injured reserve, via the Rams' website. "Semantics, mechanics of it, there was never going to be a time that he was going to return prior to anyways what I had suggested to you guys.

"So it really was not putting him on because of roster mechanics, (then) some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces."

The Rams knew that surgery was an option for Nacua. The receiver is opting to fix his injury before signing a new contract.

In the meantime, the Rams are on a bye in Week 11 while tied with the Seattle Seahawks for second place in the NFC West with 6-4 records. The San Francisco 49ers lead the division with an 8-1 record. The Rams will next host the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25.

description:

Evans was limited in both practices and is listed as questionable on the team's injury report.
"Having Mike out there -- everyone knows how good Mike is," Shanahan said.
The 49ers will have a walk-through practice at the Air Force Academy on Saturday morning before departing for Mexico.
Despite missing the past four games, Evans' 420 receiving yards still leads the team's wideouts.
text:
AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. -- Mike Evans practiced Thursday and Friday, putting the veteran receiver in position to return Sunday in Mexico City against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that he would check in with Evans on Saturday to see how the two days of practice affected the Achilles tendonitis that kept him sidelined for more than a month. Evans was limited in both practices and is listed as questionable on the team's injury report.

"Having Mike out there -- everyone knows how good Mike is," Shanahan said. "I think the guys have done a good job holding it down with him not out there, but Mike's our guy and a very unique player, and he's been doing it at a high level for a very long time. Played really unbelievable for the games he played in this year, and it'd be great to get him back."

Though some players like Evans are questionable for the game, all 53 players on the 49ers' active roster took part in Friday's practice, a rarity for the injury-addled team.

The 49ers will have a walk-through practice at the Air Force Academy on Saturday morning before departing for Mexico.

Evans was the team's top pass catcher when the season began, playing through broken ribs and becoming quarterback Brock Purdy's go-to target on third downs and in the red zone. Despite missing the past four games, Evans' 420 receiving yards still leads the team's wideouts.

He went into the Week 6 game against the Washington Commanders with Achilles tendinitis, which caused him to come out of the contest. He hasn't played or practiced since.

The 49ers dealt with a similar issue with running back Christian McCaffrey two years ago and decided to be patient with Evans, reasoning that it would be better to have him for the entire homestretch than for a particular midseason game.

If Evans, 33, plays, he'd join Deebo Samuel, 30, Demarcus Robinson 32, Brandin Cooks, 33 and Keenan Allen, 34, as thirty-something receivers available against the Vikings. Jordan Watkins, 24, and Jacob Cowing, 25, also are available for the game.

"It's awesome to have two veterans in there, two guys who have seen a lot of football," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said of the prospect of Evans and Allen playing together. "They're similar in that they're guys with size and experience and intelligence in knowing how to get open. But they have different skill sets, too, which is pretty cool."

text:
The Kansas City Chiefs will be without Kenneth Walker for the second straight week.

The star running back was ruled out of Week 11's matchup with the Arizona Cardinals due to the groin injury that kept him out last week.

Walker's absence is a big blow in fantasy football circles because of the numbers he could've produced against the Arizona defense, but the Chiefs have the bigger picture in view with the Buffalo Bills coming up on Thanksgiving Day.

There's better news regarding Baker Mayfield's health, though, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending" in the right direction ahead of their battle with the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Below is a look at all of the significant injuries affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 11.

1 p.m. ET Games

4 p.m. ET Games

Sunday Night

Monday Night

Kenneth Walker Out For Second Straight Week

The Kansas City Chiefs will have to manage without Kenneth Walker for the second straight week.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid did note on Friday that Walker is "improving" along with a few other injured Chiefs with Thanksgiving Day rapidly approaching.

Emmett Johnson ran for 110 yards, picked up 70 more yards through the air and caught a pair of touchdown passes in place of Walker in Week 10.

It's not crazy to think Johnson will produce at a similar rate in Week 11 given the matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.

The Los Angeles Rams ran for 202 yards on the Cardinals defense in Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks put up 120 rushing yards as a team in Week 9 versus Arizona.

The problem for most fantasy football players is that Johnson is no longer available off the waiver wire because of his wildly successful Week 10.

It's even harder to navigate the waiver wire in Week 11 than most weeks because six teams, including the Detroit Lions and Atlanta Falcons, are on byes.

Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans is a fascinating add for Week 11 because he faces the Dallas Cowboys' league-worst rushing defense. It's also a game against his former team for Pollard.

The Denver Broncos' Jonah Coleman is worth a look as well. He had 57 yards on 17 carries last week and goes up against a Las Vegas Raiders defense that gives up 151.1 rushing yards per game.

Baker Mayfield "Trending In Right Direction"

There's hope in Tampa that Baker Mayfield can play against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles noted on Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction"

Mayfield had plenty of time to rest during Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye ahead of an important two-game stretch for the Bucs. They face the Carolina Panthers on Monday night in Week 12 in a massive NFC South clash.

Mayfield put up 243 passing yards in Week 9 in a tough matchup with the Chicago Bears. He has another difficult matchup on his hands against a Detroit defense that improved over the last month.

The Lions won't have Aidan Hutchinson rushing the quarterback, but they still have all of the key pieces in place in the secondary. That unit allowed under 200 passing yards in each of the last three games.

There aren't many options off the waiver wire if you'd like to sit Mayfield because of the matchup.

text:
The regular season rolls on in the NFL with Week 11 already underway after the Houston Texans' victory over the Indianapolis Colts kicked things off on Thursday. Now, we have the rest of the slate on deck. While this is the smallest collection of games that we'll have this season (13) thanks to six teams being on a bye, it packs quite a punch. That includes a potential NFC Championship preview between the Vikings and 49ers in Mexico City.

Of course, as is the case with every week in the NFL, injuries are a substantial piece of the puzzle and remain a big storyline heading into each contest. This week, there are some heavy-hitters that headline the injury front. Namely, the Chiefs will once again be without star running back Kenneth Walker III, while Niners standout receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) still has his status up in the air.

As teams across the league wrap up their week of practice, they've unveiled their final injury reports along with game statuses. Below, you can find updates for every game in Week 11.

Note: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, Los Angeles (Rams), New England, and Seattle are on the bye in Week 11.

All lines via DraftKings; All times ET

Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills (-16.5)

Dolphins: P Bradley Pinion (right groin), WR Jared Wayne (quad) OUT; CB Jaylin Simpson (knee), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder, groin) DOUBTFUL; CB Darrell Baker Jr. (knee), C Aaron Brewer (concussion), CB Marcellas Dial Jr. (toe) QUESTIONABLE

Bills: CB Christian Benford (groin), LB Dorian Williams (calf) OUT; TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle) DOUBTFUL; S Damar Hamlin (toe), TE Jackson Hawes (shoulder), DL T.J. Sanders (shoulder) QUESTIONABLE

Pinion nor Wayne was able to practice this week, so seeing them ruled out by Miami isn't too surprising. The Dolphins did get some encouraging progression from Trader, who was upgraded to a limited participant during Friday's practice. That gives him a chance, despite that doubtful designation. Each Dolphins player listed as questionable practiced fully on Friday.

Benford and Williams did not practice all week and have since been ruled out. Kincaid also did not practice at all this week as he deals with thumb and ankle injuries, but the Bills are holding out some hope by not ruling him out just yet, albeit listing him as doubtful.

New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5)

Saints: CB Martin Emerson (concussion), OT Taliese Fuaga (knee), C Erik McCoy (biceps), OT Asim Richards (knee) OUT; CB Decamerion Richardson (thigh), LB Pete Werner (hamstring) QUESTIONABLE

Bears: CB Kyler Gordon (shoulder) OUT; WR Zavion Thomas (ankle) QUESTIONABLE

After being limited on Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury, Saints rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson was a full participant on Friday and carries no designation for Week 11.

Gordon did not practice at all this week for Chicago and has officially been ruled out. Meanwhile, Thomas popped up on the injury report on Friday as a non-participant due to an ankle injury that has him questionable.

Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5)

Titans: G Fernando Carmona Jr. (ankle) OUT; S Tony Adams (concussion), LB Anthony Hill Jr. (neck), CB Micah Robinson (hip), RB Tyjae Spears (knee), WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) QUESTIONABLE

Despite listing five players as questionable, the Titans are pretty healthy entering this matchup. Every one of those players was able to practice fully on Friday, which bodes well for their chances of being able to suit up on Sunday.

Outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku was a full participant Friday and carries no injury designation for Week 11. This comes after he was a non-participant on Wednesday and a limited participant on Thursday due to an ankle injury. Safety Jalen Thompson was a full participant for the second-straight day.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-5.5)

Buccaneers: CB Josh Hayes (knee), S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) OUT; OLB Yaya Diaby (knee), QB Baker Mayfield (foot, right thumb) QUESTIONABLE

Lions: C Cade Mays (ankle) OUT; LB Joe Bachie (knee), CB Khalil Dorsey (ankle), DL Tyler Lacy (shoulder), CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder), CB D.J. Reed (hip), RB Sione Vaki (ankle) QUESTIONABLE

Baker Mayfield is officially listed as questionable as the Bucs quarterback practiced in limited fashion on Thursday and Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Mayfield "had a good day today" and the team will continue to monitor him leading up to Sunday. If Mayfield cannot play, undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels would start.

Mays did not practice at all this week for Detroit as he manages an ankle injury. As for the rest of the players listed as questionable, each practiced in a limited capacity all week. Meanwhile, safety Kerby Joseph is set to make his return after practicing fully all week and carries no designation.

Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5)

Cardinals: OL Jon Gaines II (ankle), DL Zach Carter (knee) OUT; QB Carson Beck (back) QUESTIONABLE

Chiefs: OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), G Trey Smith (concussion), RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) OUT; DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), DL Peter Woods (neck)

Carson Beck did not practice on Friday as head coach Mike LaFleur noted the rookie is dealing with a back injury. As of now, the team is preparing for veteran Josh Johnson to start.

Kansas City will be without star running back Kenneth Walker III for the second straight week as he continues to deal with a groin injury. That'll thrust rookie back Emmett Johnson back in as the primary starter out of the backfield.

Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) at Philadelphia Eagles

Steelers: LB Patrick Queen (hand), WR Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), WR Roman Wilson (hand), S DeShon Elliott (knee), LB Nick Herbig (hip, ribs), G Gennings Dunker (knee) QUESTIONABLE

Eagles: WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle, foot), LB Zack Baun (back) OUT; LB Smael Mondon (ankle) DOUBTFUL; RB Will Shipley (foot, illness) QUESTIONABLE

Every Steelers player listed with an injury designation, except Nick Herbig, was able to practice fully on Friday. That includes linebacker Patrick Queen, who was limited over the first two days of practice due to a hand injury. Meanwhile, Herbig did not practice at all this week.

Baun did not practice with the Eagles this week and has been ruled out due to a back injury. On a more positive front, wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) carries no injury designation, nor does running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring). Each practiced fully to wrap up the week.

Humphrey was sent home by the team this week and has been ruled out for this contest after he made disparaging remarks about the city of Baltimore on a podcast. On the injury front, Madubuike and Hawkins were unable to practice Friday and have been ruled out.

Okereke and Simmons were unable to practice this week and have subsequently been ruled out. Tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are the only questionable players who were limited during Friday's practice (others were full participants). That marks the second straight day each was able to practice, albeit in a limited fashion, after missing Wednesday's opening session.

The most notable development on New York's injury report is who isn't on it. Geno Smith (ankle) has no injury designation after practicing fully on Friday, lining him up to start on Sunday.

Ladd McConkey has a chance to return to action this week after the Chargers wideout practiced in a limited fashion throughout the week amid a back injury. He's officially questionable.

Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10)

Raiders: DT Tonka Hemingway (stinger) OUT; K Matt Gay (right hip), DT Folorunso Fatukasi (toe), TE Brock Bowers (ankle, quad) QUESTIONABLE

Brock Bowers is officially listed as questionable as the tight end deals with an ankle and quad injury. Bowers did not practice on Wednesday, but was able to get on the field in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday.

Denver is pretty healthy coming into the weekend. Lohner is ruled out, but practiced fully this week, while Jones was limited with a hamstring injury.

Jaguars: DE B.J. Green (forearm), C Robert Hainsey (knee) OUT; DT Matt Dickerson (neck), Danny Striggow (concussion)

Giants: No injuries to report

All eyes were on running back Bhayshul Tuten after he missed Thursday's practice with ankle and foot injuries. However, the back was able to return as a limited participant on Friday and carries no injury designation for Sunday's contest.

The Giants are extremely healthy entering Week 11, as no player was given a game designation.

There are still seven games left on the schedule, but New England's season unofficially and unceremoniously ended in the aftermath of Week 10. That's due to Drake Maye suffering a broken fibula, which will sideline him deep into the regular season if not for the whole year. The Patriots' chances of returning to the playoffs after a surprise run to the Super Bowl a year ago are all but out the window.

The team enters its Week 11 bye at 5-5 and is slotted as the No. 8 seed in the conference. With Maye on the shelf and Tommy DeVito poised to start the rest of the way (unless they add a free agent), the second half could be tough sledding for Mike Vrabel's team. That's especially true in December, when they'll have a three-week stretch against the Bills, Vikings, and Chiefs. Even with Maye in the fold, those were going to be tough matchups to overcome. Without their star franchise quarterback, they're borderline insurmountable.

Really, this injury to Maye changes the lens through which we need to view the Patriots. The focus shifts away from the nitty-gritty of the regular season and possible playoff position to the bigger-picture, existential topics that extend beyond 2026. Below, we'll highlight some of the ripple effects of Maye's injury, along with other pressing questions facing the franchise as they look to bounce back in 2027 with their star QB in the fold.

Are Drake Maye's extension talks impacted?

One element of Maye's injury that is worth highlighting is that it comes at a less-than-ideal time for the quarterback, who becomes extension-eligible this offseason. It's hard to imagine this injury truly derailing any sort of negotiation between Maye's camp and the Patriots front office. That said, you can't really rule it out either.

That's especially true considering Maye could be—and should be—looking to reset the market at the position. After all, he already has an MVP runner-up and a Super Bowl appearance on his résumé. That means exceeding Patrick Mahomes' $64 million-per-season rate that he recently inked with the Kansas City Chiefs. And that's on the low end, as other quarterbacks like Caleb Williams and/or C.J. Stroud could balloon that market-setting figure this offseason with their looming extensions.

When you're talking about executing the largest contract in NFL history, there could be some trepidation depending on how Maye's ankle recovers. The Patriots have also historically been known to drag out talks, most recently not signing Christian Gonzalez to his market-setting deal until just before the start of the regular season. While waiting with Maye could give them further clarity on how his ankle heals, it also runs the risk of the price going up as other QBs sign their deals.

Drake Maye has also looked like two completely different quarterbacks over the course of this season. Through the first three games of the season, Maye was in the midst of an all-time-bad Super Bowl hangover. New England got off to a 1-2 start that saw the third-year quarterback throw six interceptions and put up the league's lowest quarterback rating of 58.6. Since then, though, Maye looked closer to last year's MVP-caliber run despite the Patriots' litany of injuries. Between Weeks 4 and 10, Maye ranked third in touchdown passes (17), fifth in completion percentage over expectation (plus-4.2%), second in success rate (51.1%), third in EPA per dropback (0.20), and second in yards per attempt (8.9) among 31 qualified quarterbacks, all while being bressured at the fourth-highest rate in the league (43.6%).

Who stays and who goes in free agency?

Possibly intertwined with Maye's extension could come some hard questions regarding who stays and who goes on this current version of the Patriots roster.

For instance, this offseason New England has receiver DeMario Douglas, offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, offensive lineman Michael Onwenu, safety Kevin Byard, linebacker Christian Elliss, and receiver Mack Hollins, all set to hit free agency. On top of that group, corner Carlton Davis (would create $16.5 million in cap space if cut), pass rusher Harold Landry ($14.5 million), and right tackle Morgan Mosses ($9 million) are all potential cut candidates to clear up space.

Each of those players mentioned is, or at least has been, a key contributor to the on-field product. Hollins and Douglas are the last two receivers on the roster who meaningfully contributed to the Patriots' 2024 Super Bowl Run; Onwenu has been New England's most reliable offensive lineman over the last few years; Byard currently leads the team in interceptions, while Ellis leads the team in tackles. New England will need to either look to the draft to fill those holes or dip their toe into the free-agent market.

At the moment, Over the Cap projects the Patriots to have roughly $16.8 million in available cap space.

Even more pressure on A.J. Brown acquisition

There's really no other way to describe the A.J. Brown trade than as an utter disaster. When the Patriots shipped out a 2028 first-round pick as part of the blockbuster trade to acquire the star receiver, Brown was supposed to be the crown jewel that would take New England's offense to a new level. That hasn't materialized.

Brown has been limited to four games due to an array of injuries. He suffered a high ankle sprain early in the season, in the opening matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. That forced him on injured reserve. Then, after just two games back, a knee injury forced him to miss the club's Week 8 and Week 9 contests. To make matters even more maddening with Brown, he sufferd a third injury, leaving Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Lions early with a hamstring injury that will force him to miss multiple weeks.

So far, the wideout has suited up in four games and caught 11 of his 26 targets for 128 yards and zero touchdowns. Brown has also had three drops.

With Maye sidelined for the year, Brown faces immense pressure to produce when he's back on the field in 2027 and make last summer's sizable investment worth it. That could be a true roll of the dice, as Brown will be entering his age-30 season in 2027 and with a sizable injury history. He may not be the player he was during his early days in Tennessee or at the peak of his tenure in Philadelphia, but the Patriots will need more than what they've gotten from him next year.

If they don't, their record will likely suffer because of it and make that 2028 first-round pick that'll be awarded to the Eagles as part of the trade even more valuable.

2027 set up as make-or-break season

While Drake Maye is still just 24 years old and hasn't even stepped into his prime yet, his team will be at a crossroads next year. The core they've built around Maye faces a make-or-break season that could lead to a reset if things continue to trend in the wrong direction.

For example, A.J. Brown is signed through 2029, but has no guaranteed money remaining on his contract in 2028 and 2029. If he doesn't turn a corner next year, it'd be hard to imagine New England re-upping him, and they would likely try to move on to clear space. Free-agent acquisition and fellow wideout Romeo Doubs is in the same boat as Brown. Those are two integral pieces to the offense that could be out the door quicker than they came in, and leave the organization looking for new pieces to surround Maye with, albeit now while paying him top dollar.

With the team not owning their own first-round pick in 2028 either, it only stresses the importance of these players (and others like them on the roster) finding their footing, as no blue-chippers are around the corner if they should struggle again in 2027.

text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Tests have shown that New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fractured his right fibula -- an injury that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all, sources told ESPN.

There was no additional ligament damage, sources told ESPN, which leaves open the possibility, but hardly a certainty, that Maye could return toward the end of the season if New England is in playoff contention.

It is not the only injury news the Patriots are dealing with. They are preparing once again to be without No. 1 wide receiver A.J. Brown, whose injured hamstring is expected to sideline him multiple weeks, sources told ESPN. It will mark the third time Brown misses games this season, following a high ankle sprain in the season opener that landed him on injured reserve for four games and a knee flare-up that kept him out of games in Weeks 8 and 9.

Both Maye and Brown would normally be candidates to land on injured reserve, but the Patriots are in a rare situation because they have been ravaged by injuries across the roster this season, and are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from IR.

Teams are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from IR in the regular season and then receive an additional two to return from IR in the playoffs. The Patriots have already used five return designations and appear to have earmarked two more for starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs (scapula), who are eligible to return next week.

So that would leave just one remaining return designation in the regular season, and with others on IR -- such as speedy No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) -- the team will have to strategize how it manages its roster in that regard.

The Patriots (5-5) are on their bye week, and coach Mike Vrabel said Monday he "wouldn't imagine [Maye] being available" when the team returns to prepare for its next game -- Nov. 29 at the Los Angeles Chargers. Vrabel said backup Tommy DeVito will start in his place, and 2026 seventh-round pick Behren Morton, who has made a positive impression, is the No. 2 option.

Daniel Jones, who was released Friday by the Indianapolis Colts, could also be an option for the Patriots.

The Patriots are currently eighth in the AFC, and the top seven teams qualify for the postseason. Their remaining games are at the Chargers (1-8), followed by home games against the Buffalo Bills (8-1) and Minnesota Vikings (7-2), road games at the Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) and New York Jets (2-8), and home contests vs. the Denver Broncos (7-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-8).

Playing without Maye adds a significant obstacle to their hopes of making a playoff run. Entering last week, Maye ranked in the top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

Maye was injured in last Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, when Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked him on the final play of the first drive, landing on his right leg.

Maye was helped to his feet by teammates and limped to the sideline before walking to the locker room for further evaluation. He didn't return home with the team that night "out of caution," according to Vrabel, instead flying back the next day with other team staffers.

Brown, whose first season in New England has been sidetracked by injuries, sustained his hamstring injury in the third quarter of the game. He has played just four games this year and totaled 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns, while struggling to catch the ball consistently. He had three drops in his initial return to action in Week 6.

Vikings return four starters from injury ahead of 49ers matchup

Associated PressNovember 20, 2026 - 4:29pm

EAGAN, Minn. — The Minnesota Vikings will return four starters this week from injuries that kept them out of the previous game, with linebacker Blake Cashman, tight end T.J. Hockenson, defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins and wide receiver Jajuan Jennings all cleared to play against San Francisco.

Cashman (concussion), Hockenson (wrist), Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) and Jennings (calf) were all sidelined for the 30-10 win at Green Bay last week. None of them had an injury designation for the game in Mexico City on Sunday night after fully participating in practice on Friday.

The Vikings listed starting cornerback Isaiah Rodgers as questionable to face the 49ers with a minor quadriceps injury he suffered during practice this week. Wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) will miss his second straight game, as will quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring). Addison avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve, so he could return within the next two weeks.

text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- The Chicago Bears will be without nickel corner Kyler Gordon when they host the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

Gordon was sidelined from practice all week with a shoulder injury and subsequently ruled out on the final injury report.

He injured his left shoulder Nov. 8 while defending a deep pass to Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson in the third quarter of Chicago's win over Tampa Bay. Gordon lay on the ground for several minutes while holding his left wrist before he exited for the locker room with two trainers. He was able to return and finish the game.

Johnson characterized Gordon's injury as "day-to-day" earlier in the week but said he had no further information on its severity when asked Friday. Johnson said Chicago's stretch of two games in five days -- the Bears play at the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving -- did not factor into the decision to sideline Gordon.

"I haven't even thought about it," Johnson said.

Running back Kyle Monangai will make his return after a five-game absence due to turf toe and a thumb injury. Wide receiver Luther Burden III (concussion) is also expected to play, and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons does not have an injury designation after he was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday because of a knee injury.

Gordon made his 2026 debut in Week 6 after missing the entire spring offseason program and training camp with a calf injury. He has been one of Chicago's most productive defenders over the past month, recording four sacks and forcing two fumbles.

title: Drake Maye has fractured right fibula, will not require surgery, per report - CBS Sports
description:
The New England Patriots must move forward without quarterback Drake Maye for the foreseeable future.
Maye was officially diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.
It took multiple days for the Patriots to announce the extent of Maye's injury.
Maye's injury occurred on the first drive of the game when Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson brought him down for a sack.
Looking ahead, Maye is unquestionably locked in as the Patriots' franchise quarterback even if the injury is season-ending.
text:
The New England Patriots must move forward without quarterback Drake Maye for the foreseeable future. Maye was officially diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss. Maye sustained the injury in the Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. The injury will not require surgery, but it is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he returns at all, per Schefter and Reiss.

Maye did not travel back to the United States with the Patriots and instead remained in Germany to undergo additional postgame testing. Coach Mike Vrabel said during his weekly radio appearance that the team ordered him to stay out of caution so medical personnel could rule out anything that might complicate his air travel. The tests were also performed to determine whether he would require surgery.

It took multiple days for the Patriots to announce the extent of Maye's injury. While they reportedly had concerns by Monday that the star signal-caller had fractured his ankle, the official diagnosis was not made public until later in the week.

Maye's injury occurred on the first drive of the game when Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson brought him down for a sack. Hutchinson also suffered a serious injury on the play when he tore his right ACL during his celebration.

The NFL ruled that Hutchinson's sack was not a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting, which are required indicators of an illegal tackle. Vrabel also said he did not think it was a hip-drop.

New England's offense sputtered without Maye on the field and managed just two scores in the 35-10 loss. One of those, a field goal, came on the fateful drive shortly after Maye exited the game. Tommy DeVito entered the contest in relief and completed just 12 of his 24 passes for 81 yards. The backup quarterback threw a touchdown and an interception and ran four times for another 19 yards. He figures to handle the starting duties in Maye's absence moving forward, although Vrabel on Monday said he had not "even thought that far."

"My comfort level with Tommy is I think that he can help us if he has to play," Vrabel said. "He's been prepared. I think he's practiced well. I think he's prepared well. Probably a tall task [on Sunday]. I'm sure there's some things he would liked to have done better and given us a better chance to get in the ballgame."

The Patriots are in a fight to stay afloat in the postseason picture and are in danger of slipping out of contention during Maye's absence. The AFC East title is well out of reach since the Patriots stand 3.5 games back of the conference-leading Buffalo Bills, and they are one game out of the Wild Card race as the eighth-best team in the AFC.

Drake Maye injury the latest for Patriots amid snakebitten 2026 Super Bowl hangover

Tyler Sullivan

This is an unfortunate conclusion to a massively disappointing season for Maye, who, before the injury, played well below the near-MVP level he reached during the 2025 season and the Patriots' run to the Super Bowl. Last year's league leader in completion percentage, passer rating, and yards per attempt took sizable steps backward in each of those categories over the first 10 weeks and owns career-worst marks in completion percentage (65.6%) and interceptions (11).

While not completely ruled out for the season as of yet, New England will need a meaningful turnaround after dropping three of their last four games headed into the bye. Despite the 5-5 record, the Patriots still have a 32% chance to make the playoffs, per NFL Next Gen Stats. New England has the 12th-easiest remaining schedule by DVOA, according to FTN Network.

Here are the remaining games on the Patriots' schedule following their Week 11 bye:

Week 12: at Chargers

Week 13: vs. Bills

Week 14: vs. Vikings (Thursday)

Week 15: at Chiefs (Monday)

Week 16: at Jets

Week 17: vs. Broncos

Week 18: vs. Dolphins

If there is any silver lining, it is that the Patriots are in the midst of their bye week, which gives Maye an additional handful of days to recover without missing a game.

Looking ahead, Maye is unquestionably locked in as the Patriots' franchise quarterback even if the injury is season-ending. He will return in 2027 for the final year of his rookie contract, although he becomes eligible for an extension this offseason. Whether the Patriots elect to sign him long-term in the coming months or wait to see how he performs coming off the injury remains to be seen.

Rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and caught two receiving touchdowns last week, will once again take on the starter's role.

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL this week, head coach Sean McVay announced on Friday. The procedure will rule him out for the next few months, which could result in him missing the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

"We always thought [it] was a possibility," McVay said regarding Nacua's surgery. "It's going to be a couple months and we're going to have to go on without him."

The 6-4 Rams, who are on a bye in Week 11 and play Thanksgiving Eve against the Green Bay Packers, are currently tied for second in the NFC West and have seven more games left in the regular season. McVay did not have a definitive timeline for a return. The team is currently scheduled to play its Week 18 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Jan. 3, a game that could be flexed depending on what the playoff picture looks like at the time.

McVay did not rule out a Nacua return should the Rams make the postseason, but said, "you're planning on not having him."

Luther Burden III (concussion) has cleared protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Chicago Bears wide receiver logged three full practices this week and carries no injury designation. Same goes for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was limited this week with a knee issue. "Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he said.

Injuries that kept him limited in Wednesday's practice did not keep Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) away from being on the field Thursday and Friday. The Raiders' leading receiver exited Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks after just 11 snaps with an ankle issue. He is currently listed as questionable.

text:
New details about the severity of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's leg injury have come to light.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss, tests revealed Maye suffered a fractured right fibula that is expected to keep him out "deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all."

The report noted there is no ligament damage, nor will Maye require surgery.

Maye was injured on the opening possession of New England's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday when he was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson.

The Patriots star limped to the sideline and was later shown on the Fox broadcast walking back to the locker room.

It was initially reported the Patriots were concerned about Maye's ankle as they awaited test results, but the expectation has always been he would miss at least most of the remainder of the season.

One potential wrinkle to this situation, which Reiss and Schefter pointed out, is the Patriots only have one remaining IR return designation left to use this season.

Both Maye and AJ Brown, who is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, would be candidates to go on IR under normal circumstances.

The Patriots are still in playoff contention in the AFC with a 5-5 record. They are only one game behind the Cleveland Browns for the final wild card spot entering Week 11.

New England and Cleveland are on a bye this week, so the playoff positioning will not change. The Patriots' remaining schedule includes four games against winning teams, including the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos.

Tommy DeVito replaced Maye for the remainder of the Lions game. He went 12-of-24 for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

An undrafted free agent out of Illinois in 2023, DeVito has started eight games in his NFL career. He threw for 913 yards, seven touchdowns, one interception and completed 63.8 percent of his attempts in six starts with the New York Giants in 2023.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams knew they would be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games after he was placed on injured reserve, but now it appears that his absence will extend even longer than that. Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua had surgery on his MCL and will miss "a couple of months."

Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders. He took a handoff on third-and-11 and ran it for a 5-yard gain but was injured on the play. He was placed on injured reserve after the injury, which is apparently more serious than initially appeared, given that it required surgery.

Nacua was also suspended earlier this week for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, a suspension he will serve while on IR. The NFL did not disclose the nature of his violation, but it's believed that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.

The NFL did not know that Nacua had potentially season-ending surgery when it suspended him for three games, according to The Athletic.

Now, the Rams will likely be without Nacua for at least the remainder of the regular season. They're on their bye in Week 11 but return in Week 12 to take on the Green Bay Packers in a Wednesday game the night before Thanksgiving. They'll close out their season with games against the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Seahawks again.

The Rams are likely to get fellow wide receiver Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson back from injured reserve when they return from their bye, or shortly after that. Adams has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury, while Ferguson has been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury and then a hamstring ailment he suffered during his 21-day practice window.

The Rams will desperately need each of them to play significant pass-catching roles, as last week they were left with only Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, rookie CJ Daniels and practice-squad signee Xavier Smith at wide receiver. That's alongside Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen and Max Klare at tight end for their victory over the division rival Arizona Cardinals.

description:

text:
Puka Nacua's season is likely over.

The Rams' star receiver decided to undergo surgery on his injured MCL on Tuesday and will miss a couple of months, coach Sean McVay told reporters Friday.

"I kind of thought when the initial injury occurred that this was more [than] likely the direction that this would go," McVay explained Friday. "So this isn't anything necessarily new on our end. It's just more of he had to get some different information, talk to people. ... I did think that this was a possibility.

"That was a serious injury that he sustained, whether he got it fixed or not. ... In my mind, this was kind of always the direction that we had to plan upon anyways."

With eight weeks remaining in the regular season, it's probable Nacua won't be ready in time to return to the field unless the Rams mount a deep playoff run, meaning the surgery brings an anticlimactic end to Nacua's fourth NFL season. It was a campaign in which Nacua was arguably never more important to the Rams, becoming a do-everything receiver who averaged 10 catches per game and also began moonlighting in various secondary roles solely out of necessity for the banged-up Rams.

It was also one fraught with health challenges. Nacua battled psoas issues prior to the start of the regular season, missed two games with a hip issue before returning in Week 4, sustained a calf injury during practice in late October and saw his season indefinitely interrupted when he suffered a knee injury and turf toe in Los Angeles' win over Washington in Week 9. The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve following the latest pair of injuries, ruling him out for at least a month before Friday's news.

Nacua's prior off-field conduct also attracted frequent attention during the 2026 season. The NFL officially suspended Nacua for three games earlier this week, effective immediately, meaning he'd serve the suspension while on IR. Multiple reporters from various outlets (including NFL Network and ESPN) have since reported the league was unaware that Nacua had undergone surgery prior to the three-game ban.

In total, 2026 has been a winding journey filled with examples of Nacua's premier value as a playmaker, as well as questions about how he'll fit into Los Angeles' future. Nacua is approaching free agency this offseason and will likely command top dollar on the open market, which would make the franchise tag a viable solution in order to keep him in Los Angeles for at least one more year. But with his growing injury history, his off-field issues and the Rams' checklist of pending free agents, Nacua's situation and outlook isn't exactly certain and will be worth monitoring closely in the early months of 2027.

text:
The New England Patriots spent their bye week without a firm answer on Drake Maye, and the outlook has not improved since he was helped off in Munich. The team fears its starting quarterback has a fractured ankle, and he is out indefinitely and possibly for the rest of the 2026 season, ESPN’s Adam Schefter said on Wednesday in an interview with WEEI, as NESN reported.

NFL Network had reported on Monday that Maye could miss the rest of the season with a significant lower-leg injury, NFL.com said.

Table of Contents

Drake Maye injury update: what we know

Confirmed: Maye was hurt on New England’s first drive against the Detroit Lions in Munich on Nov. 15, when Aidan Hutchinson rolled onto his ankle on a sack. He did not return, and Detroit won 35-10.

Reported: the Patriots fear a fracture. Maye stayed in Germany after the game for more tests to decide whether he needs surgery.

Confirmed: coach Mike Vrabel does not expect him back for the first game after the bye. “I wouldn’t imagine him being available coming out of the bye,” Vrabel said on Monday.

Not confirmed: whether Maye will have surgery, and any return date. The team has not announced either.

What Vrabel has said

Vrabel has avoided a timeline. He said the club would wait to see the test results and how Maye looked once he was back in the United States, and would do what is best for his health. That leaves the Patriots planning week to week rather than for a set return.

Who plays quarterback for New England

Backup Tommy DeVito finished the Lions game after Maye went down, and the offense managed little once Maye left. Vrabel has said he is comfortable with DeVito if he has to start.

New England returns from the bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Los Angeles Chargers. If the fracture is confirmed and Maye needs an operation, DeVito is likely to start most, if not all, of the remaining games.

Why it matters for the Patriots

Maye finished second in the 2025 MVP voting and is the center of everything New England does on offense. The Patriots went into the bye at 5-5 and in the race for the last AFC wild-card spot, so losing him for a long stretch could decide their season.

text:
Adam Schefter doesn't have the answers Patriots fans want.

Nearly a full week after quarterback Drake Maye left New England's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich with an ankle injury, there have been few official updates on his status.

"I think he's got some type of fracture in his ankle. I think he's going to be out indefinitely, if not for the season," Schefter, ESPN's resident NFL insider, told WEEI's "Rich, Ken, and Ted" on Wednesday.

"It's a devastating injury for them, a brutal blow for him, the team, everything. That's where their season took a major turn."

That's been the gist of the updates — or lack thereof — from the Patriots, who left Maye behind in Germany for an extra day as he received medical treatment.

On Monday, coach Mike Vrabel didn't offer up much to reporters, and there likely won't be anything official with New England in its bye week.

"I'm not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here," he said. "He's en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people, and they're en route back here. So, once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer. But I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye."

That does not appear good enough for Patriots' super fan Bill Simmons, who vented his frustration on X.

"It's officially been three days since Drake Maye may or may not have broken his ankle," The Ringer founder tweeted Wednesday.

Schefter showed signs of exasperation during the WEEI hit at the sheer amount of unanswered questions surrounding Maye and the Patriots, who will go forward with Tommy DeVito as their starter, backed up by Behren Morton for the foreseeable future.

What is the exact nature of his injury? Will Maye require surgery? Is a return this season possible?

"Everybody's being very careful about it. They get very sensitive about these things — understandably so," he said as tension in his voice broke through. "I'm telling you, it's a fractured ankle, he's out indefinitely. What more are you looking for? Specifics — we're trying to get them, but what more do you need to know than he's out indefinitely.

"He's out indefinitely, if not for the season. I don't know yet. There are more details that are missing, but the macro is the macro and he's out. They're going to have to make do without him for a while."

Just how long, though, is literally anybody's guess — even the NFL's biggest news breaker.

text:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was scheduled to be a full participant at practice Friday and appears on track to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday (4:05 p.m. ET on FOX).

Smith twice left the Jets’ 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, first to be evaluated for a head injury late in the first half and then after he hurt his left ankle during his only series of the third quarter. He was limited at practice earlier this week, but said Wednesday he intends to play.

"He'll be practicing fully today, so we'll see how that goes," coach Aaron Glenn said before practice Friday. "He looks solid. It's very encouraging."

The Jets (2-8) are looking to snap a five-game losing streak when they face the Chargers (1-8), who got their first win when they beat the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

Smith was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik last week. The fourth-round pick from Clemson would make his first NFL start if Smith can’t go, but that doesn't appear to be the case this week.

Glenn said the team would see how Smith, left guard Dylan Parham (knee), defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) get through practice Friday before making final calls on their availability for the game at Los Angeles.

"We've got two days to see how these guys operate," Glenn said. "It is looking promising for all these guys, so I feel good about that."

The offense will be down two wide receivers, though, with Glenn ruling out rookie Omar Cooper Jr. with ankle and hip injuries and Isaiah Williams with a rib injury. Neither was expected to practice Friday after sitting out the other practice sessions this week. Both were hurt against Buffalo.

The Jets have Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Tim Patrick and rookie Malik McClain as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Sterling Shepard and Jamaal Pritchett are on the practice squad. Tight ends Mason Taylor and rookie Kenyon Sadiq could also see increased targets in the passing game.

"I think that's the good thing about the tight end room is those guys can actually end up playing some of those receiver spots that we have," Glenn said.

Williams is the Jets' primary punt returner, so Isaiah Davis could assume that role. Williams also shares kickoff duties with Kene Nwangwu.

Defensive lineman David Onyemata, on injured reserve the past eight weeks with an abdominal injury, won't be activated from injured reserve this week, Glenn said. The Jets opened Onyemata's 21-day practice window on Wednesday, so they have two more weeks before they need to either activate him or place him on season-ending IR.

Nacua was also suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, but he is being allowed to serve the suspension while on IR.

This does seemingly end Nacua's regular season. He has played seven games, recording 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

There is some good news for the Rams on the receiver front. McVay said on Nov. 11 that Week 13 is a "realistic timeline" for Davante Adams to return from a ruptured hamstring he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6.

The Rams are on bye this week and will host the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve to kick off Week 12. Their Week 13 matchup is against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday Night Football.

text:
Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.

Hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration. He tore his knee when he landed.

Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season, dealing a significant blow to the Lions' hopes of making a run through the playoffs. On Thursday, Hutchinson released a statement about the injury, his recovery and his future celebration plans via his Instagram account.

"I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me," Hutchinson wrote. "But even something like this won't hold me back."

In the wake of the injury, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said that he's retiring his backflip celebration because of what happened to Hutchinson. And now, Hutchinson himself says he won't be jumping in the air in celebration anymore, either.

"Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger," Hutchinson said. "2. That's the last time I go airborne 😁👍"

Hutchinson getting injured while celebrating his sack meant that he joined a sneakily extensive list of players suffering unusually-timed injuries, such as Lamarr Houston, Stephen Tulloch and Bill Gramatica, each of whom also tore their ACL while celebrating a play.

Hutchinson's injury probably won't stop everyone in the league from celebrating in the air, but if it inspires even a few more players to stop going airborne, that'll probably be for the best.

Dan Campbell won't tell his players to stop celebrating

For what it's worth, Lions coach Dan Campbell said that even in the wake of Hutchinson being lost for the season, he won't tell his players to stop celebrating on the field.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore,'" Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket.

Campbell also recalled a story from his own playing days while again stating that he won't tell players to stop celebrating their on-field accomplishments.

"No, I don't believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself," Campbell said. "We're not talking to 8-year-olds here. And I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.

"This game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."

Campbell is a firm believer in building the personality of your team. It's clear that he doesn't want to change his team's personality — which has been built in his own image over the years — even in the wake of a devastating injury.

text:
The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs.

Beck was officially listed as limited for practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, with a back injury. He was later present in the locker room while it was open to reporters, and appeared to be walking around without discomfort. The injury report was first released shortly after the locker room closed to reporters.

This is not the first time Beck has had back trouble this season, as he dealt with a back injury for two weeks in October. That injury first surfaced on Oct. 16. He missed two practices the following week and was listed as a limited participant three times, before returning to full participation on Oct. 29. Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then.

“He’s just dealing with a bit of spasms,” head coach Mike LaFleur said on Oct. 23, of Beck’s previous injury. “It’s not like a long-term (issue) or anything like that. But trying to throw the way these guys throw, if you’re having a little bit of a back tweak, that’s what’s going on with him.”

LaFleur’s next press conference is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, two days before the Cardinals’ game against the Chiefs in Kansas City.

If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week.

The bigger concern, though, would be the impact on Beck’s development, after an encouraging NFL debut in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) If ever there was a time for an NFL team to overlook somebody, it just might be Sunday afternoon at Arrowhead Stadium, where the Kansas City Chiefs will continue their pursuit of another AFC West title against the injured, downtrodden Arizona Cardinals.

The Chiefs (7-2) have moved back into first place in the division thanks to tiebreakers over the Broncos, who have an identical record through the first nine games. But a slip-up against the Cardinals (3-7) could be downright disastrous considering the Chiefs are staring at a five-week meatgrinder that includes the likes of first-place Buffalo, Cincinnati and San Francisco.

“They've had a lot of injuries, obviously, but they still have a lot of NFL talent on the roster,” Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill said. “At this point, the message is just about us stacking wins in November and December, and we're going to try to do that on Sunday.”

The Chiefs have bounced back nicely from back-to-back losses in Seattle and Denver, taking advantage of what was long perceived to be the soft part of their schedule. They blew out the Jets 35-12 at home a couple of weeks ago, and they beat the Falcons by an almost identical 35-13 score last week - their fifth win by at least two touchdowns this season.

Even without ailing running back Kenneth Walker, and injuries along their offensive line, the Chiefs have been able to score at a high clip. Patrick Mahomes is playing like an MVP again, throwing five touchdown passes last week in Atlanta, and the acquisition of wide receiver Josh Downs in a trade with Indianapolis is already paying dividends for Kansas City.

Its defense has been stingy, too, holding Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson in check last week.

Juxtapose that with the Cardinals, who were waylaid 34-6 by the Rams last weekend.

Arizona put safety Andrew Wingard and linebacker Jordan Burch on injured reserve this week, pushing their total to 16 players on injured lists, tied with the 49ers for most in the NFL. That includes quarterback Gardner Minshew II, first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, fellow running back Trey Benson, wide receiver Michael Wilson and offensive tackle Paris Johnson II.

The injury to Minshew means that Carson Beck will make his second consecutive start this week. The third-round pick out of Miami endured a rough NFL baptism last weekend, going 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions against the Rams.

“It’s us coming up with the best plan possible to put these guys in position to be successful, and then them going and executing the job," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said. "Every single guy, if you ask them - if they have a jersey and they’re in the National Football League, they’re going to tell you they belong, and they’re going to tell you that they can make the plays.

"They have another opportunity this week to get that done.”

Arizona (3-7) at Kansas City (7-2)

When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS.

Latest odds: Chiefs by 15 1/2.

Against the spread: Cardinals 4-6, Chiefs 5-4.

Last week: Cardinals lost to Rams 34-6; Chiefs beat Falcons 35-13.

Last meeting: Chiefs beat Cardinals 44-21 on Sept. 11, 2022.

Series record: Chiefs lead 10-3-1.

Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson against the Cardinals run defense, which allows 129.9 yards per game, fifth worst in the NFL.

Walker is expected to miss his second game because of a groin injury, which means the fifth-round pick out of Nebraska will once again be the featured back. Johnson filled in on short notice last week in Atlanta, running for 101 yards and catching six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He has 519 yards from scrimmage this season, second most among all rookies.

The Cardinals, meanwhile, have allowed at least 120 yards rushing in six of their 10 games, and they were especially bad against the Rams. Blake Corum ran for 100 yards, Ronnie Rivers ran for 81, and the Rams finished with 202 yards rushing as a team.

- The Chiefs have won five of the past six in the seldom-played series. They are 4-0 against the Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium.

- Chiefs TE Travis Kelce has caught a pass in 200 straight games, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. The longest streak by a tight end in NFL history is 211, set by Tony Gonzalez.

- Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut in Atlanta. The Chiefs acquired him for a pair of draft picks from Indianapolis early last week, and he should be more comfortable with a full week of practice this week.

- Chiefs WRs Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each caught their first career touchdown pass against the Falcons. Allen's was from 39 yards and Armstrong's was from 43.

- Beck will be facing a former MVP and Super Bowl-winning quarterback for the second straight week in Mahomes. Beck faced the Rams' Matthew Stafford in his first career start last week.

- Cardinals S Budda Baker is the only player who was on the team when they last visited Arrowhead Stadium in 2018.

“I don’t anticipate any issues with him,” Allen said, per Cronin.

It will be a busy week for the Bears. After hosting the Saints, they have a short-week visit to the Lions for the early game on Thanksgiving.

Simmons has played two games for the Bears since being traded from the Titans. He has a sack in both of those contests.

If Simmons gets another sack on Sunday, he’ll be the first Bears player to get a sack in each of his first three games since Khalil Mack in 2018.

text:
In his first public comments since suffering a torn ACL sustained while leaping into the air to celebrate a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake May, Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson vowed to “come back stronger” and never “go airborne” again in an Instagram post on Thursday, Nov. 19.

Four days after Hutchinson’s season was ended by a celebration gone wrong during the team’s 35-10 win over New England in Munich, Germany, Hutchinson let the fanbase hear from him and addressed blowback about his decision to sky into the air in celebration, which resulted in his knee buckling underneath him.

Similar celebrations have taken out several players since the turn of the century, including an infamous local instance in which Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch was lost for the remainder of the 2014 season.

“I honestly can’t believe it,” Hutchinson began. “I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me.

“But even something like this won’t hold me back.

“I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why, and I always trust him.

“Very grateful for your prayers and well wishes,” Hutchinson said.

Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown said on his podcast, “St. Brown Bros,” earlier this week that he and Hutchinson, along with running back Jahmyr Gibbs, all practiced the celebration, used by many pro soccer players over in Europe, after Saturday’s practice at the FC Bayern Munich Campus.

Across the league and among fans, Hutchinson drew considerable criticism for continuing to do a celebration that had taken out several NFL players, specifically an ex-Lion.

Hutchinson is also known for a move popularized by soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo, the “Suiii,” where he leaps into the air, spins 180 degrees, then lands and explosively thrusts his arms out. In a video posted by the Lions’ social media team after a sack against the New Orleans Saints in the season opener, Hutchinson does the move, and many fans begged him to stop.

“Two things I know for sure:,” Hutchinson’s statement continued.

1. I always come back stronger.

2. That’s the last time I go airborne,” Hutchinson said, concluding his second note with a smiling emoji and a thumbs up.

“Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys,” he finished.

It’s the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson has suffered a season-ending injury. In 2024, he missed the final 12 games of a season in which Detroit went 15-2 because of a broken tibia and fibula.

With the win against New England, Detroit (7-2) moved into first place in the NFC North, but will find themselves with the difficult task of surviving without All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell, who’s out indefinitely with a neck injury that occurred on Nov. 1, and Hutchinson, one of the highest-paid defensive players in the NFL.

title: Puka Nacua's suspension exposes a far bigger NFL problem - 12th Man Rising
description:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was suspended for three games by the NFL on Thursday, but he won't miss any games that he otherwise would have missed anyway.
This isn't about what Nacua allegedly did, but about the league not starting his suspension after his return from injured reserve.
The Rams could have suspended Nacua if the team thought its image suffered from whatever the wide receiver did, but that's not how the NFL works normally.
Still, a team missing a player already out with an injury shouldn't be able to benefit from the NFL having a concurrent suspension.
It looks as if the league doesn't really care about the matter and only hands out the suspension to appease public perception.
text:
Do not adjust your computer screens. What you are about to read about a player who plays for a Seattle Seahawks rival is true. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was suspended for three games by the NFL on Thursday, but he won't miss any games that he otherwise would have missed anyway.

The punishment for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, covers part of the period of time that Nacua is on injured reserve for a knee injury and turf toe. The only real punishment Nacua will face is financial, and therein lies the rub.

The NFL is implying that it cares more about money than about truly punishing those who might have done bad things away from the field. This isn't about what Nacua allegedly did, but about the league not starting his suspension after his return from injured reserve.

NFL's suspension of Puka Nacua doesn't have much teeth

The Rams certainly benefit from this weird rule because they will get their best receiver back in the same amount of time as they would have. Nacua's injury could keep him out longer than the minimum of four games he has to serve. Not that the team did this necessarily, but if there was any inkling that Nacua was going to be suspended, placing him on IR actually helped LA.

If the league really wanted to take a stance that it cared about what NFL employees did to others away from the football field, it wouldn't have a rule that allows a suspended player to serve time while on IR. That seems illogical.

The only real loss for Nacua is that he will miss the paychecks of those games he wouldn't have been playing while injured. His per-game salary is $320,389, so he will ultimately be fined $961,167. That might affect what Nacua does for dinner, but not much else.

The Rams could have suspended Nacua if the team thought its image suffered from whatever the wide receiver did, but that's not how the NFL works normally. The league is in charge of doling out punishment. The money that Puka Nacua gives up will go to charitable causes, so at least there is some good in that.

Still, a team missing a player already out with an injury shouldn't be able to benefit from the NFL having a concurrent suspension. The player gets to return when he normally would, and his life isn't changed much. The team is better off.

While the entire matter might simply have been collectively bargained over between players and the league, the truth is that everyone should care more about how the NFL looks when they suspend a player who wouldn't be playing in the first place. It looks as if the league doesn't really care about the matter and only hands out the suspension to appease public perception.

title: Sen. Blunt Rochester pushes NFL for blood clot policy after Hurts injury - WDEL
description: The blood clot injury that ended Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' season hit close to home for Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware).
text:
The New Castle County Vocational Technical School District i…

Thanks to the generosity of WDEL's listeners and advertisers…



Congresswoman Lisa Blunt Rochester delivered her final scheduled address on the House floor as a member of the House Tuesday, December 17th

The blood clot injury that ended Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' season hit close to home for Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Delaware).

Blunt Rochester lost her husband Charles to a pulmonary embolism, when blood clots reached his heart, and she said when she learned of Hurts' injury "my stomach dropped."

According to the American Lung Association, pulmonary embolisms affect 1 in 1,000 people, and is the third-leading cause of heart-related death in the United States.

With that in mind, Blunt Rochester said she wrote to National Football League Commissioner Roger Goodell asking what policies were in place to protect players from situations like Hurts, who suffered blood clots during a game in London, and then flew back to the United States.

"This is a severe medical issue, and one that people need to take seriously," she said in a social media post on Thursday.

She said the NFL and the NFL Players Association will do a joint review with independent experts to see if they need to consider further league-wide policies on the topic.

text:
HOUSTON -- Texans defensive end Chris Braswell suffered a serious-looking knee injury on the opening kickoff of Thursday night's game against the Indianapolis Colts.

As the ball was being returned by the Colts, Braswell collided with Indianapolis defensive end Caden Curry and his leg buckled, sending him down to the ground immediately.

A medical cart came out for Braswell, and payers surrounded him while an air cast was placed on his right leg. The 25-year-old, a second-round pick of Tampa Bay in 2024 after playing at Alabama, had his head in his hands and a towel covering his face as he was driven off the field.

The Texans ruled him out shortly after.

Thursday night was Braswell's first time playing in a Texans uniform after landing on their practice squad Sept. 1. He was promoted to the active roster earlier in the offseason before being waived and returning to the practice squad.

He was elevated to the active roster ahead of Thursday night's game.
